title: Quasi-compact field points have monomorphic representatives
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $X$ an algebraic space over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], with field-valued point classes and atlas topology [def-a1-space-point-topology] and sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. A field is as in [def-weil-field] and its spectrum as in [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. A field-valued morphism $u:\operatorname{Spec}F\to X$ is quasi-compact if for every affine scheme $U\to X$ the scheme $U\times_X\operatorname{Spec}F$ is quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme]. Assume every field-valued morphism to $X$ is quasi-compact. Then for every $x\in|X|$ there exist a field $F$ and a quasi-compact monomorphism $j:\operatorname{Spec}F\to X$ representing $x$. Monomorphism means that composition with $j$ is injective on morphisms from every algebraic space over $S$.

proof.text: Put $X_0=j_!X$ over $Z=\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ using [lem-sfb-space-change-base-to-integers](1)-(2). Its displayed formula identifies a field map into $X_0$ with a field map into $X$ together with its map to $S$. It also identifies point classes: equality after a common extension into $X_0$ forces equality of the structure maps to $S$. Every affine scheme map $T\to X_0$ supplies a map $T\to S$. By the fibre-product comparison in (1), its pullback against any field map is the same underlying scheme as the pullback over $X$. Hence every field map into $X_0$ is quasi-compact by the hypothesis. After constructing a field monomorphism into $X_0$, its composite to $S$ makes it an $S$-map; (2) recovers the corresponding map into $X$. Thus we may work over $Z$ and return to $S$ at the end.

Fix the point $x$ and choose a point-surjective etale scheme atlas $V\to X_0$ by [lem-a1-space-affine-etale-cover], then $v\in V$ above $x$. Let $L=\kappa(v)$ and $T=\operatorname{Spec}L$, with $i:T\to V$ and composite $b:T\to X_0$. The point-class convention [def-a1-algebraic-space-point-classes] says $b$ represents $x$; [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-from-spec-field] supplies $i$. The new Mathlib leaf [lem-sfb-residue-field-point-monomorphism] says $i$ is a scheme monomorphism. Form $P=T\times_{X_0}V$ and $H=T\times_{X_0}T$. These are schemes: each is a pullback of the representable diagonal on a scheme product [def-trf-algebraic-space]. The atlas scheme-test definition makes $P\to T$ etale. Since $b$ is quasi-compact and $T$ is affine, the affine test $T\xrightarrow b X_0$ gives quasi-compactness of $H$.

proof.text: The map $m:H\to P$ sends a pair $(t_1,t_2)$ to $(t_1,i(t_2))$. It is a monomorphism of schemes: if two maps into $H$ have equal composites to $P$, their first coordinates agree, and their second coordinates agree after $i$, hence agree by its monomorphism property; the fibre-product universal property makes the maps equal. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-etale-fibre-discrete-separable-points] to $P\to T$ at the unique point of the field spectrum: its scheme fibre is $P$, so $P$ is a disjoint union $\coprod_{a\in A}\operatorname{Spec}L_a$, with finite separable $L_a/L$. By [lem-sfb-monomorphism-into-field-coproduct], $m$ identifies $H$ over $P$ with the union of a subset of those components. The sheaf fibre-product universal property used here is [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers].

source.place: Tag 03JU (lemma-R-finite-above-x), proof (2) to (3), using schemes.tex Tag 03DP (lemma-mono-towards-spec-field) and morphisms.tex Tag 02GL (lemma-etale-over-field).

proof.text: The components of $H$ in step 3 are disjoint open subsets covering $H$. Quasi-compactness from step 2 gives a finite subcover, so only finitely many components occur. Their inclusion into $P$ is an open immersion. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation](1)-(2), the first projection $H\to T$, its composite with $P\to T$, is etale. It is quasi-compact because $T$ has only the opens $\varnothing,T$, whose inverse images are $\varnothing,H$. The interchange isomorphism $(t_1,t_2)\mapsto(t_2,t_1)$ of the self-fibre product exchanges the projections, so the second projection is etale and quasi-compact as well. Its inverse is the same interchange map, directly by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers].

source.place: Tag 03JU (lemma-R-finite-above-x), proof (2) to (3), finiteness and etaleness of the self-relation projections.

proof.text: Both projections of $H=T\times_{X_0}T$ now satisfy [lem-sfb-finite-point-self-relation-field-monomorphism], applied over $Z$. It gives a field $F$ and a map $j_0:\operatorname{Spec}F\to X_0$ representing $x$, injective on morphisms from every test scheme. This implies the monomorphism property on all algebraic spaces: if $a,c:E\to\operatorname{Spec}F$ have $j_0a=j_0c$, evaluate at every scheme $W$ and every section $e\in E(W)$. The two resulting scheme maps $W\to\operatorname{Spec}F$ have equal composites with $j_0$, so are equal. Thus $a_W=c_W$ for all $W$, and $a=c$ since algebraic-space morphisms are natural transformations [def-trf-algebraic-space].

source.place: Tag 03JU (lemma-R-finite-above-x), implication (3) to (4); scheme-test to algebraic-space-test monomorphism by the natural-transformation definition.

proof.text: Return to $S$ by [lem-sfb-space-change-base-to-integers](2): the composite $\operatorname{Spec}F\xrightarrow{j_0}X_0\to S$ makes $j_0$ a morphism of pairs, hence an $S$-morphism $j:\operatorname{Spec}F\to X$. The field-class identification in step 1 shows it represents the original $x$. If two $S$-morphisms from an algebraic space have equal composites with $j$, the corresponding maps of pairs have equal composites with $j_0$, so step 5 and faithfulness of the equivalence make them equal. Finally $j$ is quasi-compact by the original assumption on every field-valued map to $X$, on all affine scheme tests. This proves both required properties. If $|X|$ is empty, there is no $x$ to choose and the assertion is vacuous.
